leads.title: HB7 - Gender-Affirming Care, Abortion and Sexual Orientation Protections Act (2023)
leads.documents: Legally codifies, protects and defends gender affirming care, abortion, sexual orientation protections and sexual reassignment surgery for adults on request without restrictions, including for interstate travellers; basis for 'sanctuary state' status for transgender youths
leads.detail: Formally passed New Mexico Legislature March 2023 and signed by Governor Michelle Lujan Grisham; no URL visible in article text

leads.title: 2019 Birth Certificate / Driver's License Gender Designation Law - repeal of 1984 surgery requirement
leads.documents: Allows transgender people to change legal gender to male, female or neutral 'X' on birth certificates, driver's licenses and state IDs without sex reassignment surgery; establishes forms and parental consent rule for minors
leads.detail: Passed NM Legislature supermajority 26-13 House and 33-14 Senate March 2019, signed by Gov. Michelle Lujan Grisham, effective Nov 1, 2019; implements NM Dept of Vital Records 'Request to Change Gender Designation on a Birth Certificate' and MVD 'Request for Sex Designation Change'; no URL visible

leads.title: An Act Relating to Human Rights - New Mexico anti-discrimination law
leads.documents: Bans unfair discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity in employment, housing, credit, public accommodations and union membership; later amendments remove 15-employee exemption and explicitly include local entities/counties/schools/universities
leads.detail: Effective July 1, 2003; 2019 repeal bill passed 59-0 House 36-0 Senate signed by Gov. Lujan Grisham effective July 1, 2019; March 2023 loophole-closure bill signed with emergency clause; 1985 Gov. Toney Anaya executive order on public employment cited as predecessor; no URL visible

leads.title: New Mexico Hate Crime Law
leads.documents: Directly and explicitly covers violence and hate crimes committed solely based on actual or perceived race, religion, color, ancestry, national origin, gender, sexual orientation or gender identity
leads.detail: In effect since 2003; no URL visible in article text

leads.title: Elane Photography v. Willock - New Mexico Supreme Court (2013)
leads.documents: Enforcement precedent for anti-discrimination machinery: upheld claim against photography studio that refused same-sex commitment ceremony in 2006; held enforcement did not violate photographer's free speech rights
leads.detail: NM Court of Appeals three-judge panel unanimous June 2012; NM Supreme Court unanimous Aug 22, 2013; U.S. Supreme Court declined appeal April 7, 2014; no URL visible

leads.title: SB 121 - Conversion Therapy Ban (2017)
leads.documents: Prohibits sexual orientation change efforts (conversion therapy) on minors
leads.detail: Sponsored by Sen. Jacob Candelaria and Rep. G. Andres Romero; Senate 32-6 Feb 16, 2017, House 44-23 March 15, 2017, signed by Gov. Susana Martinez April 7, 2017 effective July 6, 2017; no URL visible

leads.title: HB68 Omnibus Crime Bill - repeal of gay and trans panic defence (2022)
leads.documents: Repeals common-law gay and trans panic defence
leads.detail: Passed NM Legislature Feb 2022, signed by Gov. Michelle Lujan Grisham March 9, 2022; prior standalone bills passed Senate 40-0 in 2019 and 41-0 in 2021 but died in House; no URL visible

leads.title: Gender-Neutral Single-Occupancy Restrooms Law (2019)
leads.documents: Requires New Mexico businesses and public facilities with single-occupancy restrooms to mark them as gender-neutral available to any person regardless of gender identity or sex
leads.detail: Passed 54-12 House and 23-15 Senate March 2019, signed by Gov. Lujan Grisham effective July 1, 2019; no URL visible

leads.title: HB31 - Repeal of Newspaper Publication Requirement for Legal Name Change (2023)
leads.documents: Repeals archaic requirement to publish formal change of legal name on birth certificate in newspaper, cited as privacy/safety risk for transgender individuals
leads.detail: Passed NM Legislature March 2023, signed by Governor of New Mexico; no URL visible

leads.title: Albuquerque Human Rights Ordinance Amendment and Governor's LGBTQ Data Executive Order
leads.documents: City-level enforcement alignment prohibiting discrimination based on sexual orientation, gender identity and pregnancy status; state-level executive machinery for establishment and keeping of LGBTQ data, statistics, demographics/records from LGBTQ residents
leads.detail: Albuquerque City Council vote May 2024 on recommendation of Albuquerque Human Rights Board; SB316 lapsed 60-day 2021 session, replaced by Governor executive order Aug 2021; External links cited: 'LGBT Rights in New Mexico - via Equaldex' and 'New Mexico's Equality Profile - via Movement Advancement Project'; no direct URLs visible
